cues.en: In the first part, I'll blaze through the language intro and get to the meat of it. So that's me on all the social things. This is us. I actually don't have internet right now, so I can't show you the website. But we track historic video game prices. So if you collect old school video games, you should check us out. Anyway, that's because I don't have internet, I think.
cues.zh: 第一部分我会快速过一下语言介绍，直接进入核心内容。这是我的各个社交账号。这是我们团队。我这里现在其实没连上网，所以没法给大家展示网站。但我们是做老式电子游戏历史价格追踪的。如果你也收藏怀旧游戏，可以关注一下我们。总之，我觉得连不上网大概就是这个原因。

cues.en: I'll narrate the pieces that you use your imagination instead of the internet. So we used to do back, you know, back when internet was books. Okay, so we're a polyglot shop. We have all these languages in production and we've had prologue in production for about 18 months now. So this talk is about some cool things that we've learned, things that we like and things that we don't like. Some background on prologue as a language. It is based on first order logic. Prologue is probably the most popular language in the logic programming family.
cues.zh: 我会用讲解代替网络演示，大家就发挥想象力吧。就像以前那样，在互联网还是一本本书的年代。好了，我们是一家使用多种语言的公司。我们在生产环境里用到了所有这些语言，而且 Prolog 在生产环境已经跑了大概 18 个月了。所以今天的演讲主要分享一些我们学到的酷炫技巧、我们喜欢的地方，以及我们不喜欢的地方。先讲点 Prolog 这门语言的背景。它是基于一阶逻辑的。Prolog 大概是逻辑编程家族中最流行的一门语言了。

cues.en: And it's been around for quite a while. The first version of Prolog came out the same year as the first versions of Smalltalk and C. Pretty productive year for programming language development. And because it's been around for quite a while there, I would guess maybe half a dozen language implementations that would be good for production use. We use SWI Prolog, which I'll talk about sort of why we chose that later.
cues.zh: 它存在的时间已经相当长了。Prolog 的第一个版本和 Smalltalk 以及 C 语言的第一版是在同一年问世的。对编程语言的发展来说，那真是相当高产的一年。正因为历史悠久，我猜大概有五六种语言实现都能达到生产级别的可用度。我们用的是 SWI-Prolog，稍后我会讲讲我们选择它的原因。

cues.en: One of my favorite things about logic programming specifically is how ridiculously simple the execution model is. You have basically four pieces, four moving parts, I guess you'd say. You have logical and, logical or, you have term rewriting, and then you have unification, which is a fancy pattern matching mechanism. And based on combining those four fundamental pieces, you get all computation that you care about.
cues.zh: 说到逻辑编程，我最喜欢的特点之一就是它的执行模型简直简单得不可思议。你手头基本上就只有四个构件，或者说四个活动部件。也就是逻辑与、逻辑或、项重写，再加上合一（unification），其实就是一种高级的模式匹配机制。只要把这四个基础构件组合起来，你就能实现你关心的所有计算。

cues.en: which is pretty neat. I'll show you a quick demo of sort of what Prolog looks like. A lot of your development happens at what we call the top level, what most other languages would call a REPL. A capitalized thing is a variable that represents something whose value you don't know yet. Equal represents unification. Lowercase things represent symbols. We call them atoms. Other languages call them keywords.
cues.zh: 这非常巧妙。我给大家快速演示一下 Prolog 大概长什么样。大部分开发都是在我们所谓的顶级环境（top level）中进行的，大部分其他语言称之为 REPL。首字母大写的标识符是变量，代表你尚不知道具体值的东西。等号表示合一。小写开头的表示符号，我们称之为原子（atoms），其他语言里叫关键字。

cues.en: So here I just asked Prolog does a equal foo, and it hopefully says, well, if a equals foo, then a equals foo. Maybe not really useful, but I can ask it. So does a equal foo and does a equal bar? And Prolog says that that's not possible. That's because in Prolog values are immutable. So once the value a has the value foo, it can't have any other value. And a previous talk talked about some of the benefits of that. Probably most of you already know.
cues.zh: 所以在这里我刚问了 Prolog：A 等于 foo 吗？它很配合地回答：好吧，如果 A 等于 foo，那么 A 就等于 foo。这可能没什么实际用处，但我还可以接着问：那 A 既等于 foo 又等于 bar 吗？Prolog 就会说这不可能。这是因为在 Prolog 里值是不可变的。所以一旦变量 A 绑定了值 foo，它就不能再拥有其他值了。前面有场演讲提到了这么做的一些好处，可能你们大多数人也早就知道了。

cues.en: Prolog also has compound terms. This is a way of bundling pieces of data together. So an atom followed by an open parenthesis creates a compound term with two pieces and I can I can unify those two terms.
cues.zh: Prolog 也有复合项。它把若干数据片段打包在一起。所以一个原子后面跟一个左括号，就创建一个包含两个部分的复合项，而我可以把这两个项合一。

cues.en: And Prolog will say, you know, if I make these assignments, then what you asked for is true. Now, these data structures can become arbitrarily complex. So, you know, you can unify two trees, and the pieces that match between them will come out. One other important piece here in Prolog is I might ask, so does x equal a semicolon's logical disjunction, so, or, or maybe foo of x equals foo of 7, let's say. Oops.
cues.zh: Prolog 会说：如果我做这些赋值，那么你问的东西就为真。现在，这些数据结构可以变得任意复杂。所以你可以合一两棵树，它们之间匹配的部分就会显现出来。Prolog 里另一个重要的点是我可能会问：x 是否等于 a；分号表示逻辑析取，也就是“或”，或者比如 foo(x) 等于 foo(7)。哎呀。

cues.en: So Prolog says, well, if x equals a, then the thing you asked me is true. And it pauses here for a moment, saying there may be more solutions. But it hasn't gone any effort to find them yet. It will lazily evaluate those as I ask for them. So if I press semicolon, it'll go ahead and find the other solution. So you can see here that Prolog is dynamically typed. x could be an atom. It could be a string. It could be an integer, whatever. I can tell Prolog, I guess that's going to be wrapped a little bit.
cues.zh: 于是 Prolog 说：如果 x 等于 a，那么你问我的东西就为真。它在这里暂停一下，表示可能还有更多解。但它还没费力去找。它会在我需要时惰性地求值这些解。所以如果我按分号，它就会继续去找另一个解。这里你可以看到 Prolog 是动态类型的。x 可以是原子，可以是字符串，可以是整数，随便什么。我可以告诉 Prolog……我猜那部分会稍微折行。

cues.en: tell Prolog, well, I only care about the integer solutions, and it will only find the ones that I asked for, or the ones that meet my full constraints. So in Prolog, all of your code lives inside of a database. And you can query that database just like you would any other database. This particular predicate listing queries the database and then generates the code on the screen. So here I have this silly little predicate called Baz. I can run it. It gives me.
cues.zh: 告诉 Prolog：我只关心整数解，它就只会找我要求的那些解，或者满足我全部约束的那些解。所以在 Prolog 里，你所有的代码都存在于一个数据库中。你可以像查询任何其他数据库一样查询这个数据库。这个特定的 listing 谓词会查询数据库，然后在屏幕上生成代码。这里我有一个傻乎乎的小谓词叫 Baz。我可以运行它。它给我……

cues.en: values 1, 2, or 3. But because it's just a database, I can modify it. So I can tell Prolog, well, Baz of 4.0 is also true. And if I run that, you can see that my code is there. And if I list it, you can see this very last clause down here. It's in there. So I modified my database. Now, my code is just living in the database, which is kind of cool. We'll show some more neat tricks with that later. One last intro piece I wanted to give with Prolog is
cues.zh: 值 1、2 或 3。但因为它只是一个数据库，我可以修改它。所以我可以告诉 Prolog：Baz(4.0) 也为真。如果我运行它，你能看到我的代码就在那里。如果我列出它，你能看到最下面这最后一个子句。它就在里面。所以我修改了数据库。现在我的代码就住在数据库里，这挺酷的。后面我们还会展示一些更巧妙的技巧。关于 Prolog，我想最后介绍的一点是

cues.en: to describe to you maybe the way you think about writing stuff in Prolog. In most functional languages you think of, if I have this value, how do I map it to some other value? In imperative languages you think of kind of like do this, then do this, then do this. In Prolog what you ought to think about is what are the relationships between things. So imagine I have a list of values here, and I have a list of values here, and if I put those two lists together, append them together, then I get a third list.
cues.zh: 大概描述一下在 Prolog 里写东西时该怎么思考。在大多数函数式语言里，你会想：如果我有这个值，怎么把它映射到另一个值？在命令式语言里，你会想：做这个，然后做这个，然后做这个。而在 Prolog 里，你应该想的是：事物之间有什么关系。想象这里有一个值列表，这里还有一个值列表；如果我把这两个列表放到一起，把它们追加起来，就会得到第三个列表。

cues.en: Well, in prologue, we think of that as simply a relationship between three lists. And any number of lists could meet the requirements of that relationship. So I could say, if I have a list A and a list with B and C in it, what happens if I append them? Or what is the list L which satisfies that constraint? And it's just the one that you would think. But because this is a relationship, you can run it in every different direction you can imagine.
cues.zh: 在 Prolog 中，我们把这单纯看作三个列表之间的关系。只要满足这个关系的要求，任意数量的列表都可以。所以我可以说，如果我有一个列表 A，以及一个包含 B 和 C 的列表，把它们拼接起来会发生什么？或者说满足这个约束的列表 L 是什么？答案正如你所想。但正因为这是一种关系，你可以朝你能想到的任何方向去运行它。

cues.en: So I'm asking what list F stuck onto the front of BC gives me ABC? Prolog says list of A. I thought there was another solution. Turned out when I asked for it, there wasn't actually one there. But you can even, I won't do all the combinations, but you can do cool stuff like what two lists appended together give me the list ABC? And Prolog says, well, all of these ones would work. I want you to think for just a second in your favorite programming language,
cues.zh: 所以我在问，把什么列表 F 拼在 BC 前面能得到 ABC？Prolog 说，列表 A。我本以为还有另一个解。结果等我再问时，发现其实没有了。但你甚至可以，我不会把所有组合都演示一遍，但你可以做一些很酷的事，比如：哪两个列表拼在一起能得到列表 ABC？Prolog 会说，这些全都可以。我想让大家用自己最喜欢的编程语言想一想，

cues.en: And what would it take to define the full relationship between these three lists? How much code did you have to write in order to get all these different modes of operation? And after you've thought about that, this is the full listing in Prolog. Two lines gives you all of those pieces. Now, it's OK if you don't understand how this works. You can do your homework later and figure it out. But when you really understand what your relationship is,
cues.zh: 要完整定义这三个列表之间的关系需要怎么做？为了实现所有这些不同的运行模式，你得写多少代码？想好之后，来看一下 Prolog 的完整代码。只要两行，就能搞定所有这些功能。如果你现在看不懂它是怎么运行的也没关系。你可以回头再做功课研究清楚。但当你真正理解了你的关系是什么时，

cues.en: You need almost no code at all, and Prolog will run those relationships in all sorts of different directions. Less code is better, generally, as long as it's understandable. And we found you can do some really neat things when you're working with less code. There's the piece in there where I said x equals a or foo of x equals foo of 7. That logical or highlights one of the key
cues.zh: 你几乎不需要写什么代码，Prolog 就会在各种不同的方向上运行这些关系。通常来说代码越少越好，只要它易于理解。而且我们发现，代码越少，能做出的东西反而非常惊艳。前面我说过 x 等于 a 或者 foo(x) 等于 foo(7)。那个逻辑或凸显了 Prolog 运作的核心机制之一，

cues.en: pieces of how prologue works, which is backtracking. So when prologue said x equals a, that would be one solution, and I said, well, maybe give me some more solutions. It said, OK, well, let me forget about a. Let me jump back to before I found that solution for you. Let me find a different one. If I had internet, I would show you a cool video of the video game Braid. Have any of you played Braid?
cues.zh: 那就是回溯。当 Prolog 说 x 等于 a 作为一个解，而我说“要不再给我几个解”时，它会说：“好，那先忘掉 a。让我跳回到为你找到那个解之前的状态。我来找个别的解。”要是现在有网，我就能给你们看一段电子游戏《时空幻境》（Braid）的精彩视频了。你们有人玩过 Braid 吗？

cues.en: a platformer? Sweet. A whole bunch of prologers who've played Braid. That shouldn't surprise me. For those who haven't played Braid, since I can't show the demo, imagine that you're playing like Super Mario Brothers, and you're running along, and you come to this pit. You can either jump over the pit, or you can jump into the pit. Well, maybe if you jump into the pit, there will be like secret coins down there. Or maybe you'll just die. And you don't really know until you try it. So when you come to that pit, you face a choice. And in prologue, we call it a choice point. And in prologue, you just
cues.zh: 一款平台跳跃游戏？太棒了。一整群玩过 Braid 的 Prolog 程序员。我早该料到的。对于没玩过 Braid 的人，既然我没法放演示，就想象一下你在玩《超级马里奥兄弟》之类的游戏，你一路往前跑，遇到了一个坑。你可以跳过这个坑，也可以跳进坑里。跳进坑里的话，底下也许会有隐藏金币。或者你可能直接就死了。你不试一下是不会知道的。所以来到这个坑前，你面临一个选择。在 Prolog 中，我们称之为选择点（choice point）。而在 Prolog 里，你只要

cues.en: try both. And you're like, let's jump into the pit and see what happens. So you jump into the pit and then you die. But instead of going back to the beginning of the level, prologue just says, whoa, whoa, hold on, pause the machine, reverse the machine to before I made that decision, undo everything that has happened. Let me stand on the edge of the cliff and let me jump over this time. Like, OK, I survived that time. Now I can proceed forward. Kind of all prologue execution is based on that basic idea and this backtracking notion of being able to do some stuff.
cues.zh: 两边都试一下。你会想，跳进坑里看看会发生什么吧。于是你跳进坑里，然后死了。但 Prolog 并不会让你回到关卡开头，而是说：“等等，暂停机器，把机器倒退到我做决定之前，撤销刚才发生的一切。让我站在悬崖边上，这次我选择跳过去。”就像是：“好，这次我活下来了。现在我可以继续前进了。”可以说整个 Prolog 的执行，都是基于这个基本思想，以及这种能够尝试探索的回溯概念。

cues.en: and then undo it if it's wrong is really, really powerful. I think most of you have encountered this in one way or another in database transactions. You begin a database transaction, you go through doing a bunch of stuff that you think is going to work, and then you find out something was wrong. One of your assumptions was wrong. Well, you roll back, and there were no bad consequences to that. The database isn't hurt. There's no inconsistency there. That's an essential piece to the way that Prolog can work, and you can use it for some neat tricks. That was going to be the braid video, which
cues.zh: 然后再在出错时撤销，这真的非常强大。我想你们大多数人都在数据库事务里以某种方式遇到过。你开启一个数据库事务，做一堆你认为会成功的事，然后发现有问题。你的某个假设错了。于是回滚，没有任何不良后果。数据库没受损，也没有不一致。这是 Prolog 能工作的关键部分，你可以用它做出一些巧妙的把戏。那本来会是 braid 视频的内容，它

cues.en: We still can't see. So for all the lispers out there, Prolog is one of only a few languages that really is homo-iconic. A lot of languages claim that they are, but don't quite have the same feel as you would get in Lisp. In Prolog, you really do. So in this demo, I'll just show you real quick. So this is just a compound term, right line hello. It's just data.
cues.zh: 我们还是看不到。所以对所有 Lisp 程序员来说，Prolog 是少数真正具有同像性的语言之一。很多语言声称自己具备同像性，但感觉并不太像 Lisp 里那样。在 Prolog 里，你真的能感受到。所以在这个 demo 里，我快速给你们展示一下。这就是一个复合项，对吧？line hello。它只是数据。

cues.en: I can display it to the screen. I can unify against it. But it's also code. I can execute it. And this is more powerful than just stringing down JavaScript or something. It's actually taking data and saying, well, this is your abstract syntax tree, sort of. And if you execute that tree, you get the results you want. For an example, there's a predicate called plus.
cues.zh: 我可以把它显示到屏幕上。我可以对它做合一。但它也是代码。我可以执行它。这比只是拼一串 JavaScript 之类的东西更强大。它实际上是拿数据说，嗯，这算是你的抽象语法树。执行这棵树，你就能得到想要的结果。举个例子，有一个谓词叫 plus。

cues.en: which does exactly what you would think it does. There's a predicate called map list, which is just functional map. So here I'm going to give it, I'm going to say, okay, add one, two, let's say like one, two, and what's the result? Well, the result is two, three. That's really trivial. But because Prolog is homo-iconic, you sort of get closures for free. So this plus one, even though it looks like a closure, something you might do in Haskell or in,
cues.zh: 它做的事和你想的完全一样。还有一个谓词叫 map list，它就是函数式的 map。这里我给它，我会说，好，add one two，假设就是 one、two，结果是什么？结果是 two、three。这很琐碎。但因为 Prolog 具有同像性，你相当于免费得到了闭包。所以这个 plus one，虽然看起来像闭包，像是你会在 Haskell 或

cues.en: enclosure, any functional language, it's actually not. It's really just a data structure. It's just a compound term plus with the argument one. And map list, the predicate, takes the arguments of each of those lists and it tacks them onto this data structure, builds a bigger data structure, and then executes that data structure as if it was code. And then so you get, you know, it looks just like a closure, but it's sort of not.
cues.zh: Clojure，或任何函数式语言里会做的事，但它其实不是。它真的只是一个数据结构。它就是一个复合项 plus，参数是 one。而 map list 这个谓词，会取出那些列表里每一项的参数，把它们贴到这个数据结构上，构建出更大的数据结构，然后把这个数据结构当作代码来执行。于是你就得到，你知道，它看起来就像闭包，但又不完全是。

cues.en: in maybe the technical sense. But one of the really cool things about this is that because Prolog just views all this data as code, code as data, we can get all the same benefits that you would expect from a relational style of programming. So here, I'm just asking Prolog, what would I add to one and two to get two and three? And it says, well, obviously, you would add one.
cues.zh: 也许在技术意义上不是。但这件事真正酷的一点是，因为 Prolog 把这些数据都看作代码，代码也看作数据，我们就能获得你在关系式编程风格中期待的所有好处。所以这里，我只是问 Prolog：我要往 one 和 two 里加什么，才能得到 two 和 three？它说，嗯，很明显，你会加 one。

cues.en: This is really powerful. When you can use it well and you define your relationships well, you can write code once and get like three or four different views on the same thing. It's really pretty slick. But that, I think, largely stems back to some of the benefits you get there are because Prolog is so iconic. So enough intro to Prolog. This is actually what we do in production.
cues.zh: 这非常强大。当你能用好它、把各种关系定义清楚时，你只需写一次代码，就能从三四个不同的角度来看待同一件事。这真的很巧妙。但我认为，这很大程度上归功于 Prolog 自身的标志性特色所带来的优势。关于 Prolog 的介绍就先说这么多。接下来看我们在生产环境中实际是怎么用的。

cues.en: Of all the, you know, half dozen different prologue implementations, we chose to use SWI prologue, partly because they have the best development tools that I'm aware of. Some of the commercial systems may have better ones, but we preferred something open source where we can fix bugs as we come along. And they have all the things you'd care about, like a debugger and an editor and different analysis tools and things. But I wanted to show you the debugger, because it's one of my favorite.
cues.zh: 在已有的五六种不同的 Prolog 实现中，我们选择了 SWI-Prolog，部分原因是据我所知他们拥有最棒的开发工具。有些商业系统可能会更好，但我们更倾向于开源的方案，这样遇到 Bug 就能随时修复。而且你关心的功能它全都有，比如调试器、编辑器以及各种分析工具等等。但我特别想给你们展示一下它的调试器，因为这是我的最爱之一。

cues.en: Prolog as a language probably makes me smile more often than any other language. And when I first saw this, reversible debugging, it was like my dream come true. So here's a little demo. I wrote a predicate called Hi. It should be true for any atom, which is four characters or smaller. And it's obviously broken because Hi is short, but it's not saying that it is. So I'm going to go ahead and run this in the debugger.
cues.zh: Prolog 作为一门语言，可能比其他任何语言都更能让我会心一笑。而当我第一次见到这种“可逆调试”时，感觉简直就像梦想成真一样。这里有一个小 Demo。我写了一个叫做 Hi 的谓词。它对任何长度小于等于四个字符的原子都应该为真。但它显然出 Bug 了，因为 Hi 很短，它却没判定为真。所以我现在要在调试器里运行它。

cues.en: And I apologize for some of you at the very back. This is as big as I can make this text here. So you'll have to bear with me. So I think for a minute, all of you in your favorite language, in your favorite debugger, you've all sort of been through this process where you know something's busted. cues.en: Saved states. Saved states are fun. Who has used small talk images or Dart snapshots or a few people? These are my favorite production trick from Prolog ever. So this is what a saved state does. Imagine you have your Prolog interpreter and you say, OK, Prolog, I want to run this file over here. So it loads up the file. It pulls in all the modules that you've got.
cues.zh: 保存状态（Saved states）。保存状态很有意思。谁用过 Smalltalk 镜像，或者 Dart 快照？有几个人用过？这是我在 Prolog 中最喜欢的生产环境绝招，没有之一。保存状态的作用是这样的：想象一下你有一个 Prolog 解释器，你说：“好的 Prolog，我想运行这边的这个文件。”于是它加载该文件，引入你所有的模块。

cues.en: It parses them, it compiles them, it does whatever optimizations it's going to do to the bytecode. And then right before it's going to run your code, it says, whoa, hold on, pause right there. It takes a snapshot of your whole interpreter and saves it to disk. And then it can go on doing whatever it wants, or it can quit right there. So once you have that file, it's this single fully packaged version of your code. And you can run all your tests against it. And if it passes, you just throw that file up on a server somewhere.
cues.zh: 它解析代码、完成编译，对字节码做各种优化。然后，就在它即将运行你代码的前一刻，它说：“等等，先暂停在这儿。”它为整个解释器生成一个快照并保存到磁盘上。之后它可以继续做任何想做的事，或者直接就地退出。一旦你有了那个文件，它就是一个完整打包好的独立代码版本。你可以针对它跑完所有测试，如果通过了，你直接把那个文件扔到某台服务器上就行了。

cues.en: and you know that your server is running the exact same code that you wrote because it's...
cues.zh: 而且你心里很清楚，服务器上运行的绝对就是你写出来的同一份代码，因为它是……

cues.en: bundled up in this little file. And another nice thing, if you run in environments where your code has to start and restart a lot, all the compilation and loading has already happened. You don't worry about that, because you did all that beforehand, and it's all bundled up in your little package. It's really neat. I'm playing around with a way to use library spawn and save states.
cues.zh: 都打包在这个小文件里。另一个好处是，如果你的运行环境里代码需要频繁启动和重启，编译和加载都已经提前完成了。不像某些语言，你把东西扔到服务器上，然后还得指望网络正常，好从某个 Ruby gems 之类的地方拉取这些东西。你不用操心这个，因为你事先都做完了，全都打包在你的小包里。这真的很妙。我正在琢磨一种使用 library spawn 和 save states 的方法。

cues.en: to spawn off computations on foreign servers, on remote servers. And you have some questions. You want to make sure that that cost model is apparent to your users. cues.zh: 在外部服务器、远程服务器上 spawn 计算。你会有一些疑问。你需要确保用户能清楚地看到成本模型。但从概念上说，这和 Unix 机器上 fork 一个进程没有区别。你相当于创建自己的副本，然后继续执行。没有理由不能这样做：生成一个 save state，把它发到云上某台服务器，让它通过消息队列之类的方式通信运行，从而创建自己的副本。

If you're coming from an imperative background, or if you're hiring developers that are coming from an imperative background,
cues.zh: 不过，这些人里有很多确实绝顶聪明，这很酷。但这依然是一个小生态。有些你习以为常的工具，比如 Coverity，大概就没有针对 Prolog 的静态分析支持。他们支持很多其他语言，但没有 Prolog。并不是说你不能做静态分析，你其实可以用 Prolog 做一些非常酷的静态分析。只是生态跟不上。另一个问题是学习曲线。如果你有命令式语言的背景，或者你招的开发者来自命令式背景，

cues.zh: 他们上手 Prolog 会经历非常陡峭的过程。这不是因为他们不是优秀的程序员，而纯粹是因为思维方式完全不同。很多时候，他们会在 Prolog 里写出非常具有命令式风格的代码。这并不是你真正想要的。我的意思是，它能运行，也许能完成任务。但真不该这么写，他们没有发挥出这门语言的优势。如果你有函数式编程背景，这就容易多了。如果你的团队里已经有很多函数式程序员，这种过渡对你来说会愉快得多。

cues.en: Before I started using Prolog in production, the language I'd been working on a lot previously was Haskell. cues.en: All those languages are beautiful in their own way. But when you're writing prologue, you know, like sit down and hold its hand and tell it nice things, like work with it like you like it. And I was reading a book called The Art of Prologue by Leon Sterling.

cues.en: Forget his first name, Shapiro. Anyway, toward the end of their book, they had this chapter on different structures. And in the heading, in the index, it said, difference map. cues.zh: 另一位作者叫 Shapiro，我忘了他名字叫什么。反正，在书的快结尾处，有一章讲差异结构。在索引的标题里写着“差异映射”。我就想，这应该挺巧妙的。我打赌它肯定特别声明式、特别优雅。整段代码居然只有三行。简直太美了。我就坐在那儿。说实话，我当时是在马桶上。我在那儿坐了太久了。我当时就想，哇，这也太绝了。太漂亮了。

cues.en: Prolog is based on logic. In logic, you have true and you have false. They're equal citizens in the world. Neither one is bad. They're just different, one from another. And so when something fails in prologue, it assumes that, well, you must want the answer false. Like, you must want me to tell you that this thing you thought was true is not true. Well, oftentimes it's far more like, I don't know, asking your two-year-old
cues.zh: Prolog 是基于逻辑的。在逻辑的世界里，有“真”也有“假”。它们地位完全平等。谁都不算坏。它们只是彼此不同而已。所以当 Prolog 里的某些东西失败时，它会默认：好吧，你肯定想要“假”这个答案。就像是：你肯定是想让我告诉你，你以为是真的东西其实不是真的。但在很多时候，这感觉更像是……我也不知道怎么形容，就像让你两岁的

cues.en: son to like clean his room and he'll just sort of stand there and he'll look at you and he'll say, no. Like, what do you mean? No, go clean your room. No. And you sit there and you're trying to think like, why would he say no? Like, why is this so hard? And sometimes prologue is like that. Sometimes trying to convince it to do what you want is like working with an obstinate two year old. You've just written 10,000 lines of prologue code and you type in go or whatever and it just says false.
cues.zh: 儿子去收拾房间，他就站在那儿看着你，说：“不”。你就会想：“什么叫‘不’？快去收拾房间！”“不。”你坐在那儿琢磨：“他为什么会说‘不’呢？怎么就这么难呢？”Prolog 有时就是这样。有时候想让它按你的意图去做，就像是在对付一个倔强的两岁小孩。你刚写好了一万行 Prolog 代码，输入 go 之类的运行指令，结果它就只冷冰冰地回一句：false。

cues.en: And you're like, oh, you're killing me. Give me a stack trace or something. Throw me your bone. Now, the debugger makes that easier. It's a little bit nicer because you can just run through it real quick, look for red, do retry. But it's not as nice as I would like. I wish there was a way that somehow failure could leave little hints behind. And if that failure reached the top level, you could say, whoa, let's back up. I haven't figured that out. Hopefully somebody will. But it's kind of obnoxious sometimes.
cues.zh: 你当时就崩溃了：天哪，饶了我吧，好歹给个堆栈跟踪或者什么提示吧，给点面子行不行？当然，调试器确实能帮上忙。它稍微好用一点，你可以快速过一遍，找找标红的地方，重试一下。但这依然没有达到我期望的程度。我真希望有某种机制，能让失败留下一点线索。如果这个失败传到了顶层，你就可以说：“等等，我们退回去看看。”我还没研究出怎么做。希望有人能搞定吧。但有时候，它确实挺让人火大的。

cues.en: Macros are hard to debug in probably almost every language that has them, but they're super powerful, and with great power comes great responsibility. So, I don't know, maybe great pain, one or the other. The other one is that all this magic doesn't come for free. 98% of the time in Prolog, I don't think about performance at all. But 2% of the time I do, and that's because some of this magic comes up to the surface.
cues.zh: 宏在几乎所有支持它的语言里都很难调试，但它们确实超级强大，而能力越大责任越大。所以，我也不知道，可能也意味着极大的痛苦吧，二者必居其一。另一点就是，所有的这些“魔法”都是有代价的。在 Prolog 里，98% 的时间我根本不考虑性能问题。但剩下的 2% 我必须得考虑，因为有些底层机制会浮出水面。

cues.en: In most languages, it's like 99.5% of the time. At least for me, I don't think about performance. I think about solving the problem in Prolog. That's more often than I would like. And you can still drop down to see. There's still good profiling tools if you need them. But it's something to think about. If you're doing something that's super high performance critical, you may want to think about that. Do some inch marks and things and see if that's what you want. Anyway.
cues.zh: 在大多数语言中，大概 99.5% 的时间里，至少对我而言，我是不去考虑性能的。我考虑的是用 Prolog 去解决问题。但遇到性能瓶颈的频率还是比我预期的要高。不过你依然可以降到底层用 C 语言去写。如果需要的话，这里也有好用的性能分析工具。但这确实是需要考虑的问题。如果你在做极度注重高性能的关键业务，可能就得琢磨一下了。做做基准测试之类的，看看这到底是不是你想要的。不管怎么说。

cues.en: That's the end. We're all out of time, but I'd love to talk to any of you later. Thank you for coming to the talk today.
cues.zh: 就讲到这里吧。我们的时间用完了，但我很乐意稍后和大家交流。感谢各位今天来听我的演讲。
